correctness.rationale: For every C² strictly convex body and alpha in (0,pi) with theta=alpha/pi badly approximable, the stated isoptic-chord translation operator has Fourier multiplier m_n=2e^(-in alpha)[cos(n alpha)+(-1)^n cos alpha]/sin alpha. Its n=±1 kernel is translation; n=0 is radius. For odd n=2k+1 the absolute multiplier factors as (4/sin alpha)|sin(k alpha)sin((k+1)alpha)|; for even n=2k it factors into adjacent odd half-angle cosines. The two zeros are separated modulo pi by δ=min(alpha,pi-alpha); one factor >=eta=sin(δ/2), the other >=constant*kappa/n by bad approximability, giving |m_n|>=2kappa eta/(n sin alpha). Parseval gives the H^-1 estimate. Along continued-fraction denominators q of theta, n=2q+1 has |m_n|=O(1/n); p=R+R/[2(n²-1)]cos(nt) is a smooth strictly convex support function with p+p>=R/2, so no H^-s bound with s<1. Independently tested all 4998 modes n=2..4999 for alpha=pi*(sqrt5-1)/2 against conservative finite Diophantine lower bound; smallest observed ratio >5.09. This finite test is not the proof for all n.
